name: ESTEEM
aliases: Effects of Surgical Treatment Enhanced with Exercise for Mixed Urinary Incontinence
question: Does adding perioperative behavioral and pelvic floor muscle therapy to midurethral sling surgery improve symptoms in women with mixed urinary incontinence?

design.blinding: Surgeons and outcome assessors masked; participants and therapists unmasked

arms.label: Midurethral sling plus perioperative behavioral and pelvic floor muscle therapy

design.population: Women at least 21 years old with moderately or severely bothersome stress and urgency incontinence for at least 3 months and at least one episode of each type on a 3-day diary; anterior or apical prolapse at or beyond the hymen, planned anterior or apical repair, and prior sling were exclusions.
design.locator: JAMA full text, Methods: Study Design, Patients, Interventions; Results: Study Population and Figure 1

verdictNote: Statistical superiority met; the 13.4-point symptom difference missed the 35-point clinical-importance threshold.
takeaway: In women with mixed urinary incontinence, perioperative behavioral and pelvic floor muscle therapy plus midurethral sling improved 12-month UDI symptoms slightly more than sling alone (adjusted difference −13.4 points, P=.04), below the prespecified 35-point threshold for clinical importance.

reports.label: Primary 12-month report
reports.citation: Sung VW, Borello-France D, Newman DK, et al. "Effect of Behavioral and Pelvic Floor Muscle Therapy Combined With Surgery vs Surgery Alone on Incontinence Symptoms Among Women With Mixed Urinary Incontinence: The ESTEEM Randomized Clinical Trial." *JAMA.* 2019;322(11):1066-1076. doi:10.1001/jama.2019.12467
reports.followUpLocator: JAMA full text, Abstract and Methods: Outcomes

results.measure: Adjusted mean change from baseline at 12 months; effect is between-group mean difference in change, points
results.note: Met the prespecified two-sided alpha of 0.05 for superiority, but not the prespecified 35-point minimal clinically important difference.
results.locator: JAMA full text, Table 2 and Methods: Statistical Analysis

results.measure: Adjusted mean change from baseline at 12 months; effect is between-group mean difference in change, points
results.note: Below the prespecified 15-point clinical-importance threshold; multiple secondary outcomes were not multiplicity-adjusted.
results.locator: JAMA full text, Table 2 and Methods: Statistical Analysis

results.measure: Adjusted mean change in daily episodes at 12 months; effect is between-group mean difference in change, episodes/day
Any additional treatment for lower urinary tract symptoms by 12 months
results.note: Adjusted odds ratio; denominators are eligible randomized participants.

harms.note: All 480 randomized women were included in adverse-event assessment; group counts were 242 and 238.

harms.note: New or worsening symptom through 12 months.

harms.locator: JAMA full text, Table 4 and footnote c
harms.note: Sling release, mesh excision, or cystotomy operations.

delivery.label: Sling route
delivery.value: Retropubic or transobturator midurethral sling was allowed in both groups.
delivery.locator: JAMA full text, Methods: Interventions and Randomization

delivery.label: Behavioral intervention
delivery.value: One preoperative and five postoperative visits through 6 months with centrally trained interventionists; pelvic floor training, bladder training, voiding education, and stress/urgency control strategies.
delivery.locator: JAMA full text, Methods: Interventions and Randomization

delivery.label: Efficacy follow-up
delivery.value: 416/464 eligible women had postbaseline efficacy data (209 combined, 207 sling alone); 402 were assessed at 12 months (198/235 eligible combined, 204/229 eligible sling alone).
delivery.locator: JAMA full text, Results: Study Population and Figure 1

reports.label: Corrected treatment-failure analysis
reports.citation: Sung VW, Richter HE, Moalli P, et al. "Characteristics Associated With Treatment Failure 1 Year After Midurethral Sling in Women With Mixed Urinary Incontinence." *Obstet Gynecol.* 2021;138(2):199-207. doi:10.1097/AOG.0000000000004444

results.measure: Subjective failure, objective diary failure, or additional urinary treatment at 12 months
results.note: 112/379 (29.6%) met the composite; this was a planned pooled-cohort analysis, not an arm comparison. Subjective failure used a 26.1-point UDI minimal clinically important difference; objective diary failure meant less than 70% improvement in daily episodes.

results.measure: Any additional urinary treatment at 12 months
results.note: 56/379 needed additional treatment; only 2 were treated for persistent stress incontinence. The abstract gives 14.7% for 56/379; ordinary one-decimal rounding gives 14.8%, so the percentage is omitted here.

results.endpoint: Prior overactive bladder medication and failure
results.measure: Adjusted odds ratio for overall failure, prior OAB medication versus none
results.note: Association from corrected multivariable analysis, not a randomized contrast.

results.measure: Adjusted odds ratio for overall failure, detrusor overactivity on cystometrogram versus none
results.note: Association from corrected multivariable analysis, not a randomized contrast.

relations.note: Both Pelvic Floor Disorders Network trials randomized perioperative behavioral therapy alongside pelvic surgery, in different patient populations.
